text:
Allison Grant: doing an arch review pass on perf-regression canary. few Qs before we sign off:
1) baseline strategy: rolling vs pinned “known-good” — what’s the default and what’s the escape hatch?
2) slice definitions: which dims are we *actually* alerting on? (model/region/gpu/etc)
3) suppression logic: how do we avoid “we suppressed it” == we missed a real regression? esp during deploy windows.

Noah Patel: thx. quick answers then can go deeper.
1) default baseline = rolling, per-slice, last 7d median (actually median of 10m medians). pinned baseline is supported for release trains / when we’re comparing RC vs last stable.
2) alert slices are constrained; we’re not doing per-runtime-build label b/c cardinality. more below.
3) suppression only affects paging; we still compute signal + annotate + open ticket when needed. no data drops.

Logan Wright: +1 on “no data drops”. from telemetry side: suppression is implemented in alerting rules / routing layer, not in metric ingestion.

Allison Grant: ok but “rolling last 7d median” can drift w/ fleet changes. how do you prevent baseline absorbing a slow regression over 2-3 days?

Nadia Rahman: we talked about this in ADR-0231. baseline is rolling but regression detector uses both:
- short window: current 30m p95 vs baseline
- guardrail: compare vs “yesterday same hour” (diurnal check) for extra confidence
and we have a pinned baseline mode for runtime RCs.

Sean Gallagher: also practical: for paging we’re looking for step changes, not slow drift. if we see gradual drift, it’s usually a capacity/contension issue and we want a ticket, not a page. we’ll have a “trend” detector that goes to Jira/Linear (non-paging).

Allison Grant: can you spell out pinned baseline mode? who sets it / when does it get used?

Noah Patel: pinned baseline is tied to a “baseline_build” config in perf-canary runner + detector. ex:
`baseline_strategy=pinned_build`
`baseline_build=runtime@1.18.3+sha.9c31f2a`
so if we’re running an RC in 5% of fleet, canary can compare RC slice vs pinned stable. mostly used during runtime release train windows or when we’re chasing a suspected regression.

Hiro Tanaka: from kernel side pinned baseline is super useful for “did kernel autotune pick something new” vs “fleet got noisier”. we can force compare to last known-good kernel set.

Allison Grant: ok. slice defs — what’s in / out? I’m worried about infinite combinations.

Thomas Baird: current proposed allowed label set (for metrics + alerts) is:
- `model`
- `region`
- `gpu_sku`
- `streaming` (true/false)
- `scheduler_mode` (pinned enum; canary only)
- `prompt_shape` (bucketed; not raw lengths)
Everything else is either:
- annotation (deploy events), or
- log/trace attribute on sampled canary requests.
Hard “no” list: `runtime_sha` as label, `kernel_id` as label, `node_id`, `pod`, `customer_id` (obv), raw `seq_len`.

Logan Wright: ^ this matches the cardinality budget we negotiated. also: `prompt_shape` is a small enum like `S/M/L` defined centrally, not freeform.

Sofia Ivanova: also clarifying on `scheduler_mode`: canary pins it (e.g. `stable_v3`) so it’s not exploding; the point is to reduce variance and make regressions attributable. customer traffic can be on experimental modes; canary is intended to be “control group”.

Allison Grant: so what happens if regression only exists in experimental scheduler? canary misses it.

Sofia Ivanova: yep, by design in v1. we can add a second canary lane later (one per experimental mode) but we’re intentionally starting with stable mode for signal quality. alternative is we add a low-volume “experimental lane” that is ticket-only.

Sean Gallagher: + from oncall perspective: I’d rather page on stable/control regressions first. experimental should not wake ppl up unless it’s catastrophic.

Allison Grant: suppression logic: I want specifics. deploy windows + cache warmups can cause noise, but we can’t mask real issues.

Nadia Rahman: suppression types we have in the detector:
A) Deploy-window suppression (timeboxed): if deploy annotation says runtime rollout in region, we suppress paging for that region/model slice for `T=45m`.
B) Warmup exclusion: we exclude first N canary runs after pod start (and after GPU reassignment) from baseline computation. still visible in dashboard as gray points.
C) Minimum sample size: no alert unless `n_requests >= 60` and `n_nodes >= 3` in the evaluation window.

Tomáš Novák: and “suppression” is only for the page. we still:
- emit a non-paging alert event to incident-bot w/ `suppressed=true`
- auto-create a “watch” ticket if it crosses threshold for > 2 consecutive windows
- keep dashboards red
So responders can see it during a deploy even if pager is quiet.

Allison Grant: how do you ensure deploy-window suppression doesn’t get extended forever?

Sean Gallagher: maintenance windows are config-managed in SRE repo, require approval to add > 2h. deploy-window suppression is automatic + fixed duration, not extendable. if it’s still bad after suppression ends, page fires.

Logan Wright: plus we log suppression reason in alert payload:
`reason=deploy_window` / `reason=warmup` / `reason=insufficient_samples`
so we can audit “we suppressed too much”.

Allison Grant: what about the “baseline absorbing regression” concern again — if something regresses and stays regressed for days, rolling median shifts and we stop alerting.

Noah Patel: couple mitigations:
- we store “regression score vs pinned last-stable” daily (not paging) so we can detect long-term drift
- for the release train we’ll temporarily use pinned baseline as default (during the week we’re doing heavy runtime churn)
- SRE will also watch the dashboard that compares week-over-week (7d ago) for key models
This is v1; we can add explicit change-point detection later.

Hiro Tanaka: also: if it’s a true regression, we usually see it as step change post-deploy, which will get caught before baseline shifts.

Allison Grant: ok. last Q: slice mismatch between baseline and current. ex: baseline computed w/ A100-heavy week, then fleet moves to H100. do we split by gpu_sku always?

Thomas Baird: yes. `gpu_sku` is mandatory. we don’t aggregate across SKUs. if sku unknown/missing, it goes into `gpu_sku=unknown` and we *don’t* page off that slice (ticket only) until fixed.

Nadia Rahman: we also require `region` mandatory for the same reason.

Allison Grant: this is good. can someone drop the doc link / section for the allowed label schema + suppression policy? want to reference it in the standards page.

Logan Wright: metric spec draft is in confluence under observability-standards → “perf-canary metric spec”. section “Label schema (allowed/forbidden)” has the table.

Sean Gallagher: suppression policy + routing is in eng-sre docs (“perf regression alert policy”). I’ll DM you the link.

Allison Grant: perfect. if we keep runtime_build out of labels, how do we attach it to alert payload reliably?

Noah Patel: canary runner includes runtime_build + git sha in trace attributes + log line, and detector enriches payload by querying the latest canary samples for that slice (last 5m). it’s not perfect but good enough for triage. plus deploy annotations give a strong hint when build flips.

Tomáš Novák: and worst case, runbook step 1 is “check dashboards + deploy annotations” before chasing ghosts :)

Allison Grant: sounds reasonable. pls make sure we explicitly say “suppression doesn’t drop data” and “timeboxed, non-extendable deploy suppression” in the design doc. otherwise reviewers will freak.

Noah Patel: will do. I’ll add that language + call out the ticket-only “trend” detector.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: and I’ll add a note that runtime_build/kernel_id are exemplars/trace attrs, not labels.

Sean Gallagher: +1. thanks all.

Slackbot: Reminder: Please avoid posting customer data in this channel. For perf-canary prompts, use the approved synthetic prompt sets only.
